question.problem:
Consider the matrix $A$ for which ${\lambda }_{1}=-2$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-1$ are eigenvalues, and

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4\end{aligned}]
$$

are the respective eigenvectors. What are the values of $a,b,c$ given that

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & b \\ c & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}a & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]{[\begin{aligned}1 & b \\ c & -4\end{aligned}]}^{-1}?
$$
question.worked_solution:
Since the eigenvalues of the matrix are ${\lambda }_{1}=-2$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-1,$ we construct the diagonal matrix $D$ by writing the eigenvalues in the main diagonal:

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, to construct the matrix $P,$ we simply write the respective eigenvectors as columns: 

- the $1$st column is the eigenvector corresponding to ${\lambda }_{1}=-2,$ and

- the $2$nd column is the eigenvector corresponding to ${\lambda }_{2}=-1.$

Therefore, we get

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ -2 & -4\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ -2 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]{[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ -2 & -4\end{aligned}]}^{-1}.
$$

 

In conclusion, we get $a=-2,$ $b=3,$ and $c=-2.$
